source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Login to OpenBMC Web GUI: Open a browser and enter the IP address or hostname of the target OpenBMC server to access the Web GUI. Sign in with your login credentials.
2. Find User Management Options: Once logged in, look for options related to user management. This may be found in the User Accounts, Permissions, Authentication, etc. sections.
3. Set up users: In the user management area, you can create, edit or manage user accounts. Make sure that the user account you set has appropriate permissions for subsequent setting operations.

4. Look for Zeroconf or Network settings: In OpenBMC's Web GUI, look for options related to Zeroconf or Network settings. This may be found in sections such as network settings, connectivity, or system settings.

5. Enable Zeroconf or mDNS: In Zeroconf or Network Settings, look for an option to enable Zeroconf or mDNS. This may have a switch or option that lets you enable Zeroconf or mDNS functionality.

6.Save Settings: After making a setting change, make sure to save the settings.

7. Restart service or system (if required): In some cases, configuration changes may require restarting network services or the OpenBMC system to apply the changes. Please refer to the relevant documentation to determine if this is required.

8 .Test Zeroconf: When you're done with the setup, other Zeroconf-capable devices should be able to discover your OpenBMC server on the same LAN.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL identifies the need for a configured BMC and Avahi client, but its password-bearing SSH wrapper disables host-key verification, checks the client daemon rather than proving the BMC implementation, and conflates DNS-SD browsing with hostname resolution.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly rejects sshpass and StrictHostKeyChecking=no, requires identity-correlated client discovery and keeps configuration authority with the operator.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 800/2291 retains PARTIAL and same-L2/operator prerequisites, but only flags shell quoting; it does not address credential exposure, the unrelated user-management step, implementation attribution or separate mDNS and DNS-SD evidence.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-965 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently adds an explicit three-layer acceptance model, stale/colliding responder controls and coverage accounting for a non-systemd-networkd implementation.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 permits an approved Project-specific tool or interface while retaining source coverage differences; ED-36 treats the hostname, service map and package as readiness inputs rather than permanent blocking; ED-38 reserves execution verdicts for engineers.

original_test_intent: Enable the approved BMC Zeroconf/mDNS function and prove from a same-link client that the intended BMC hostname and management service are discoverable. Because the Items explicitly name systemd-networkd, implementation attribution is an additional checkpoint when that wording is part of Project acceptance.
original_method: An authorized operator uses the OpenBMC Web GUI to enable Zeroconf/mDNS and applies any documented restart; a Linux client then accesses the example `<hostname>.local` URL and uses `avahi-browse`. The preserved user-management instructions are prerequisites only and do not themselves validate discovery.
manual_activity: An engineer authorizes or performs the WebUI configuration and any network-service restart or BMC reboot, verifies alternate management access, and decides whether account setup is actually required. After those inputs exist, automation may perform read-only client discovery, resolution and endpoint correlation.
required_inputs: Expected BMC hostname, `.local` name, management IP/MAC, interface/VLAN, address family and same-link topology
Expected DNS-SD service type and instance, SRV target, port, TXT records and approved HTTP/HTTPS endpoint
Authoritative platform evidence for whether systemd-networkd is the required implementation or only the source title's description
Approved BMC configuration path, least-privilege existing account or separately authorized account prerequisite, apply/restart semantics and maintenance window
Client package/version, duplicate-hostname policy, alternate management path, prior-state snapshot, rollback and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not run the DeepSeek command as written: do not expose a password through sshpass/process arguments or disable SSH host-key verification.

Do not create, edit or elevate a BMC account merely because the generic Procedure mentions user management; use an approved existing least-privilege identity unless Project SPEC separately authorizes an account change.
Snapshot network/mDNS state and prove an alternate management or console path before enabling the feature or restarting network services; a BMC reboot requires explicit approval.
Run discovery only on the approved same-link test segment; stop on duplicate hostname, unexpected responder, wrong address/MAC/service, management loss or configuration drift.
Distinguish fresh name resolution, DNS-SD service records and endpoint identity; cached `.local` data or an unrelated Avahi responder is not sufficient evidence.
Preserve BMC and client logs, do not automatically retry or clear evidence, and restore the prior mDNS/network/account state if the change is temporary.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, perform only static review and package/readiness checks; do not change BMC users, hostname, network, mDNS settings or services.
After approval, run client-side read-only mDNS resolution and DNS-SD browsing, capture interface-scoped responses and correlate addresses/services to the approved BMC identity.
Validate the advertised endpoint without assuming HTTP and HTTPS are equivalent, and collect BMC-side configuration/service evidence if systemd-networkd attribution is required.
Do not restart services or the BMC, bypass authentication/TLS/SSH identity, alter accounts, flush DUT evidence, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the actual hostname/service/interface matrix, implementation checkpoint, client package and least-privilege access model.
Apply or supervise any BMC configuration and approved restart with alternate access and rollback ready; separately authorize any account change if genuinely required.
Confirm responder identity, implementation evidence, restored configuration and final DUT verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `avahi-browse` is relevant client evidence, but the wrapper is unsafe and semantically incomplete: it can expose credentials, disables host-key verification, checks an Avahi daemon on the SSH target, and does not separately prove `.local` resolution, DNS-SD records, BMC identity or systemd-networkd attribution.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, use the test client's native resolver and an interface-scoped approved DNS-SD browser to collect the exact name, A/AAAA, PTR/SRV/TXT, target and port; correlate them to BMC IP/MAC and endpoint identity, with separate BMC-side evidence for the named implementation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The WebUI enable/save flow, conditional restart, same-LAN discovery, `http://myserver.local` example, `avahi-browse`, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONDITIONAL ON PROJECT INPUTS AND APPROVAL
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record the prior state; enable only the approved mDNS configuration; from a clean same-link client prove hostname resolution and the expected DNS-SD service independently; correlate the endpoint to the BMC; prove the systemd-networkd implementation separately if required; then restore and verify management access.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Project-defined OpenBMC network stack, mDNS/DNS-SD advertisement, management interface and same-link policy.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, network-stack/service configuration and client resolver/browser package versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC network, Zeroconf/mDNS/DNS-SD, systemd-networkd integration, user-management and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, protocol-layer and implementation checkpoints, rejects unsafe SSH credential handling, and prevents generic user-management text from causing an unapproved account change while preserving the Master procedure.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A Project-approved alternative responder or HTTPS endpoint can prove the agreed discovery function, but it cannot claim the source's systemd-networkd or HTTP-specific coverage unless equivalence and the residual gap are recorded.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Hostname/identity, service-record matrix, implementation requirement, same-link client, apply/restart and rollback plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Multicast visibility and cached records can produce a plausible response from the wrong host; network-setting changes can also remove the management path.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve another BMC configuration interface, mDNS responder, service type or HTTPS endpoint, but it must record the original WebUI/systemd-networkd/HTTP wording, the actual method, equivalent discovery coverage and any implementation or protocol coverage not exercised.
expected_evidence: Preserved Master row plus approved hostname, BMC IP/MAC/interface/VLAN/address-family and service-record matrix
Pre/post BMC network and mDNS configuration, authorization, change/restart timestamps and implementation/service-status evidence without secrets
Interface-scoped fresh `.local` resolution showing expected A/AAAA response correlated to the BMC identity
DNS-SD browse/resolve showing expected PTR, service instance, SRV target/port and TXT records, with duplicate/unexpected responders recorded
Approved HTTP or HTTPS endpoint reachability and BMC identity correlation, with protocol and implementation coverage stated separately
Client/BMC logs, alternate-management continuity, restored prior state, credential hygiene and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently targets Zeroconf/mDNS discovery. The source leaves the actual hostname, records and implementation proof unspecified, and its user-management section is overbroad, but these can be handled as Project readiness and bounded coverage rather than an irreconcilable target or acceptance contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Missing hostname, service definition, client package, configuration authority and restart plan are execution-readiness inputs. Once supplied, the discovery and identity checks are deterministic; their absence does not make the Review permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its client discovery idea but rejects the unsafe SSH construction and separates name resolution, DNS-SD advertisement, endpoint identity and implementation proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION and its credential/identity controls, while tightening account-change boundaries and the systemd-networkd coverage claim.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces its command-presence/quoting focus with a protocol-accurate evidence matrix and recovery boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps its non-blocking classification but adds explicit resolver-versus-browser acceptance, alternate-responder/caching controls and Project-override coverage accounting.

review_improvement: Prevents a cached hostname, wrong LAN responder or generic service listing from being accepted as proof that the intended BMC and the source-named implementation are discoverable, while avoiding an unnecessary credential mutation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A `.local` lookup proves name-to-address resolution, while a DNS-SD browse proves advertised service metadata; neither alone proves the responder is the intended BMC, and client-side success does not by itself identify the BMC's network backend. Those are separate, automatable observations once engineers supply identity, topology, configuration authority and recovery. Therefore the review is complete and conditionally executable rather than blocked.
